text:
The Rangers were the better team for most of this game, and the last 40 seconds of the third period made the scoreboard agree. Alexis Lafrenière scored at 18:22 on a 76% chance, then again at 18:54 on a 69% chance, turning a one-goal lead into a 5-2 win at Madison Square Garden. It was his third goal of the night, and nearly all of the Rangers' third-period edge in expected goals (2.43 to 0.23) came out in those two shots.

The game started even. NYI matched NYR in the first period on chance quality (1.22 to 1.14), and Oliver Bjorkstrand's slap shot at 6:40 was a 7% look. Lafrenière made it 2-0 at 0:25 of the second on a 4% snap shot, the least likely goal of the game. The Islanders answered with a Bo Horvat power-play goal and a Calum Ritchie wrist shot at 4:52 to tie it 2-2. From there the Rangers took over, outchancing NYI 1.68 to 0.80 in the period, and Bjorkstrand's power-play goal at 17:07 put them back in front. J.T. Miller had a 42% look in the second that Semyon Varlamov stopped.

By expected goals the Rangers won 5.25 to 2.25 (2.25 to 1.45 at even strength), and they would win this game in 75% of simulated replays. They also led in shot attempts, 56 to 47. Varlamov's 19 saves on 22 shots left him 0.8 goals above expected, so the Islanders stayed close longer than the chances said they should. Igor Shesterkin stopped 17 of 19 and broke even against the shots he faced. The late flurry made the margin look as lopsided as the play had been.
